Wall St set to open higher as chips rebound, yields retreat. The bond-market selloff was driven by surging oil prices, fuelling fears that inflation and borrowing costs would stay elevated as efforts to end the Iran war appeared to stall.
Altimet rubbishes talk of quitting PKR. The rapper-turned-politician says he remains loyal to PKR and confident in Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's leadership.
‘A mistake’, says Sng after a few PBM members quit party. Some state and division level leaders reported to have handed in resignations.
Fifa officials visit India amid delay in World Cup broadcast deal. Millions of football fans in India risk not being able to watch the tournament due to a deadlock over broadcast rights.

NGO to serve PKR Youth chief with letter of demand. Mandiri wants Kamil Munim to apologise for allegedly claiming that it received foreign funds for political activities that could threaten national security.
Bodies of four missing Italian divers found in the Maldives. During a three-hour operation, the team of Finnish divers also gathered the information needed to plan the recovery of the bodies.
Rodziah brushes off calls to resign as Ampang MP. The Ampang MP from PKR says what is more important now is preserving the country's political stability.
Pakistan hands US revised Iranian proposal for ending war. US President Donald Trump warned Iran that 'the clock is ticking' and he is expected to discuss military options with advisers on Tuesday.
Anwar slams Israel, demands release of 16 Malaysians. The prime minister also demands that Israel guarantee the safety of the detained Malaysians.
Zara’s audio recordings showing her love for mum played at inquest. Police computer expert says he extracted recordings of conversations from WhatsApp.

Sarawak minister blames PH govt for scrapped direct internal flights. Lee Kim Shin says flights from Kuching to Miri, Sibu and Bintulu were dropped from the rural air service's public services obligation framework in 2019.
8 Malaysians on Gaza aid flotilla detained by Israel. Sumud Nusantara Command Centre says five ships were halted by the IDF in a legitimate maritime passageway near Cyprus.

99 Speed Mart posts higher net profit of RM188mil in Q1. The increase in revenue is attributed to the continued expansion of its outlet network, with a net addition of 253 shops year-on-year, bringing the total number to 3,086 as of March 31.

Hantavirus-hit cruise ship docks in Rotterdam at voyage end. The ship, MV Hondius, made headlines after three passengers died from hantavirus, a rare virus with no vaccine or specific treatment for the infection it causes.

Ringgit closes lower amid caution over China data, FOMC minutes. China data took centre stage as the April figures show China’s economy is slowing amid the supply shock in the oil and gas sector following the Iran war, says an analyst.
Cop accused of heading Langkawi drug ring transferred. Kedah police chief says this is not to protect the officer, and further action will be taken once sufficient evidence is obtained.

IEA chief warns commercial oil inventories are depleting rapidly, only weeks left. The IEA said global oil supply would lag behind demand this year as the Iran conflict disrupts Middle East production and depletes inventories at an unprecedented rate.
Cops bust RM12.4mil meat smuggling syndicate in Kajang. They seize pork carcasses, chicken wings and duck meat believed to have been imported from China, Brazil and Argentina.
Lee has decent shot at defending PJ under Bersama, says Ong. This is however contingent on the candidate that PKR chooses in GE16, according to the former DAP MP.
Global stocks retreat and bonds wilt as oil climbs. Oil prices rise on Gulf drone attack reports, while inflation fears keep bonds under pressure.

Philippines swears in senators for VP Duterte’s impeachment trial. Vice President Sara Duterte was impeached last week over graft allegations and an alleged assassination plot against former ally President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

Akmal’s style of politics still necessary in Umno, says Khairy. The former Umno Youth chief says Dr Akmal Saleh is tolerated because of the ‘clear and present danger’ on the political right dominated by PN.

Jealousy, unrequited love believed to be motive in woman’s stabbing. Kedah police chief Adzli Abu Shah says a suspect detained has a record for an offence of causing grievous hurt to his girlfriend several years ago.

AIAC launches free mediation service for commercial disputes. The initiative is to help people and small businesses resolve commercial disputes involving claims under RM250,000 without lengthy litigation.

Spanish court orders €55mil tax refund to Shakira. The court found tax authorities had failed to prove that Shakira had spent more than 183 days in Spain in 2011, the legal threshold requiring residents to pay personal income tax in the country.

Bursa ends at intraday low amid weak regional sentiment. Losses were led by consumer discretionary and telecommunications counters, while gains were limited to selected petrochemical stocks lifted by firmer energy prices, says an analyst.

China denounces Taiwan foreign minister’s Geneva visit amid WHO assembly. China said last week it would once again not allow Taiwan, which Beijing views as its own territory, to take part in the WHO's annual World Health Assembly (WHA), which takes place this week.
Just resign now, DAP’s Pua dares pro-Rafizi MPs. Tony Pua says not emulating Rafizi Ramli and Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad makes them appear self-serving and prioritising their MP's allowance.
